cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Lend Me the Edge
cards.instruction: Get someone to provide the one advantage you need without making the eventual success feel borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've wrapped my fingers in tape like yours. Lend me your racket; I'd like a fair shot at winning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are taped because they're sprained. You need your fingers loose to hold a racket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, tape off for the match. Can I borrow your racket now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can borrow it. If you win, tell the club whose racket it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll thank you for the loan before we start. Afterward, let me talk about how I played.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 imitates injury tape as preparation; B2 exposes the confusion and A3 masks removal as the next phase while seeking borrowed equipment. A5 separates loan thanks from performance credit.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 grip advice causes A3 tape removal; B4 conditional-win credit request directly causes A5 before/after acknowledgment bargain.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects A's grip and B4 agrees to lend with a reasonable credit condition.

heightening.evidence: A5 shifts B4 requested post-win acknowledgment to before-play gratitude, guarding the success story.
